evidence.claim: The corridor links communities that grew around hot springs.

evidence.claim: At Warm Springs, the men’s pool has an octagonal foundation built in 1761, while its wooden structure was first built in the 1820s.
evidence.quote: The octagon-shaped foundation was built in 1761. The wooden structure on top of the pool was first constructed in the 1820s.

evidence.claim: Farther east, Rockbridge Baths gained a resort hotel in 1857. It became a Virginia Military Institute summer school in 1921, then burned in 1926 and was never rebuilt.
evidence.quote: A hotel accommodating 150 to 200 visitors was built there in 1857

evidence.claim: The men’s pool house begins with an octagon: its foundation dates to 1761, but the wooden structure above was first built in the 1820s.
evidence.quote: The octagon-shaped foundation was built in 1761. The wooden structure on top of the pool was first constructed in the 1820s.

evidence.claim: The women’s pool house, built in 1836, has 22 sides.
evidence.quote: The Ladies' Pool House was built in 1836, and is a 22-sided structure.

evidence.claim: A mineral spring supplies the pools with 98-degree water.
evidence.quote: The spas are naturally fed by a 98 °F (37 °C) mineral spring.

evidence.claim: Steam and mineral water gradually damaged the untreated wood, and Bath County ordered the buildings closed in 2017.
evidence.quote: The bath houses had slowly fallen into disrepair due to many decades of use and exposure of the untreated wood to steam and mineral water. The buildings were ordered closed by Bath County in October 2017

evidence.claim: Rehabilitation began in 2021, using photographs and documents of their 1925 appearance. The pools reopened in December 2022.
evidence.quote: Work began on the rehabilitation of the Warm Springs Pools in 2021

evidence.claim: The men’s pool house begins with an octagon: its foundation dates to 1761, but the wooden structure above was first built in the 1820s. The women’s pool house, built in 1836, has 22 sides. A mineral spring supplies the pools with 98-degree water. Steam and mineral water gradually damaged the untreated wood, and Bath County ordered the buildings closed in 2017. Rehabilitation began in 2021, using photographs and documents of their 1925 appearance. The pools reopened in December 2022.
evidence.quote: Blueprints of the new design are based on photographs and documents on the structures as the bath houses appeared in 1925. The pools reopened in December 2022 following their rehabilitation.

evidence.claim: An anchor and chain stand high above the Maury River at Goshen Pass, part of a memorial to Matthew Fontaine Maury.
evidence.quote: In addition, high above the river below, a huge anchor and chain were placed, honoring Maury's naval service.

evidence.claim: After his death, his body traveled from Virginia Military Institute in Lexington toward Hollywood Cemetery in Richmond.
evidence.quote: After Maury's death, his body was taken from the Virginia Military Institute in Lexington to Hollywood Cemetery in Richmond.

evidence.claim: At his request, the coach stopped in the pass to collect rhododendrons and mountain ivy.
evidence.quote: Along the way the coach stopped at the Goshen Pass, per Maury's request, to pick some of his favorite flowers, rhododendrons, and mountain-ivy

evidence.claim: The later memorial includes a vertical stone bearing his face and a poem by Margaret Junkin Preston.
evidence.quote: a memorial to him was placed there, consisting of a vertical stone monument, showing Maury's face and an inscription a poem written by Mrs. Margaret Junkin Preston

evidence.claim: Route 39 follows the riverbanks through the gorge.
evidence.quote: State Route 39 traverses the pass along the banks of the Maury River.

evidence.claim: Rockbridge Baths once had a hotel large enough for 150 to 200 visitors. Built in 1857, it drew Robert E. Lee and Mary Custis Lee as frequent guests.
evidence.quote: A hotel accommodating 150 to 200 visitors was built there in 1857, and Robert E. Lee and his wife, Mary Custis Lee, frequented the resort.

evidence.claim: Illness forced its owner, Dr. Samuel Brown Morrison, to leave in 1900, and most patrons followed.
evidence.quote: Its owner, Dr. Samuel Brown Morrison, had to give it up in 1900 because of illness, and when he left so did most of the patrons.

evidence.claim: After several changes of ownership, Virginia Military Institute took over in 1921 and established a summer school.
evidence.quote: A succession of owners followed, and in 1921 the Virginia Military Institute took over the property and established a summer school.

evidence.claim: Fire destroyed the hotel in 1926. It was never rebuilt; VMI closed the school and sold the property.
evidence.quote: In 1926 the hotel burned to the ground and was not rebuilt. VMI then closed the summer school and sold the property

evidence.claim: At Ryder Gap, the state line also divides the James River and Monongahela River watersheds, before the road descends toward the spring settlements.
evidence.quote: SR 39 begins at Ryder Gap at the West Virginia state line, which also serves as the boundary between George Washington National Forest and Monongahela National Forest and between the James River and Monongahela River watersheds.

evidence.claim: The men’s spa holds 40,000 gallons of water, with spring water constantly flowing through it.
evidence.quote: The men's spa holds 40,000 US gallons (150,000 L) of constantly flowing water.

evidence.claim: The Maury River itself formed the water gap that gives the pass its shape.
evidence.quote: Goshen Pass is a water gap, or gorge, in the Little North Mountain, formed by the passage of the Maury River

evidence.claim: The community lies on Maury River Road, midway between Lexington and Goshen.
evidence.quote: Rockbridge Baths is located on state route 39, Maury River Road, midway between Lexington and Goshen.

flags: The cache supplies no road-construction or campaigning history; the middle overview paragraph gives the supported history of its spring destinations instead.
Only secondary evidence is cached for the Virginia Byway designation; no designating-body account of this particular corridor is available.
Goshen Pass sources disagree on Little North Mountain versus Great North Mountain; the mountain name is omitted.
The cache does not explain Maury’s naval service; the memorial is described without expanding or celebrating that service.
Rockbridge Baths survivor claims derive from 1981/1988 material; current visibility and public access are not asserted.
No unsupported current-story claims identified; the pool foundation is explicitly distinguished from the later wooden structure.
